questions.question: What did the letters want to do at the beginning of the story?
questions.explanation: This question helps children remember the goal of the story, making it easier for them to connect the characters’ excitement to their own experiences of wanting to try something new.

questions.question: How did the letters feel when they all climbed the tree together? Was there enough room for everyone?
questions.explanation: It encourages children to think about being with friends and when things get crowded or tricky, tying the story events to feelings they might know.

questions.question: What happened to the letters when the tree fell down? How do you think they felt?
questions.explanation: Helping children talk about how the letters felt after the fall builds empathy and helps them understand a key turning point in the story.

questions.question: Who came to help the letters after they fell? Can you think of a time someone helped you when you were hurt or sad?
questions.explanation: This links the story to real life, encouraging children to make connections between receiving help and supporting each other.

questions.question: Some letters were crying or tangled after the fall. What did their friends and family do to help them feel better?
questions.explanation: This reinforces the moral about kindness and helping after something goes wrong.

questions.question: Have you ever tried something and had it not work out? What did you do next?
questions.explanation: Brings the lesson of trying again into the child's lived experience, helping them see resilience as part of their own life.

questions.question: Why do you think A wanted to climb the tree again even after everyone fell down?
questions.explanation: Asks children to think about persistence and encourages a discussion about not giving up, which is at the heart of the story’s moral.

questions.question: If you see a friend fall down or feel sad, what could you do to help them feel better?
questions.explanation: Helps children apply the moral to their everyday interactions by giving them a concrete example to think about.

questions.question: What do you think is the most important lesson the letters learned from climbing and falling from the coconut tree?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to summarize the story’s moral in their own words and discuss how teamwork and trying again are important.

moral: Even when things don't go as planned and we all fall down, we can get back up, help each other, and try again—just like the letters climbing the coconut tree.
learning_objectives: Children will be able to recall and sequence the main events of the story.
Children will discuss feelings and identify ways to help friends when something goes wrong.
Children will recognize that it’s okay to make mistakes and that they can always try again.
Children will make connections between story events and real-life situations, practicing empathy and kindness.
